article_notes: Russian methodological guidelines (LLM translation from Russian, not reviewed by a person; quotes are from the English file). Data from veterinary station reports and laboratory smear/serology in the Ryazan region; B. canis by smear morphology (and serology), D. reticulatus vector. Severity forms (severe, moderately severe, moderate, mild) are not defined, group sizes are not given and no statistical tests are described: every row is descriptive_only with low confidence. Treatment-efficacy figures are not severity associations. Breed: only a statement that the hyperacute form was noted in some breeds, with no comparison; not extracted.

severity_definitions.label: severe / moderately severe vs moderate and mild forms
severity_definitions.definition: Authors' clinical forms of the disease (severe, moderately severe, moderate, mild); criteria not stated. Other component: clinical severity form, undefined.
severity_definitions.severe_group: severe (and moderately severe) form, n not stated
severity_definitions.comparison_group: moderate and mild forms, n not stated
severity_definitions.quote: In moderate and mild disease, the above-mentioned hematological and biochemical changes in dogs are less pronounced.

associations.note: Ranges per group: severe or moderately severe 23-68 %; mild course 'low and average parasitemia values (2,5-7%)' in more than 80 % of infected dogs. The authors add that parasitaemia correlates with severity, with no statistic.
associations.quote: with manifestation of the disease in a severe or moderately severe form in a small number of dogs of the urban population (УП=23-68%)

associations.note: Young (1-2 years) and old (13-17 years) dogs had more severe disease than dogs aged 3-7 years (mostly moderate and mild). No numbers per severity group.
associations.quote: Dogs aged one to two years are often infected with babesias (more than 40%) and the disease in them takes a more severe form compared with animals aged 3-7 years.

associations.note: Narrative only: changes in the severe form vs 'less pronounced' in moderate and mild disease (the abstract says 'not significant', with no test described). Group sizes and per-group values not given.
associations.quote: in dogs with the severe form of babesiosis there are erythropenia, decreased hemoglobin, hematocrit and platelets, leukocytosis
